patients.label: Woman in her 70s with IgG multiple myeloma and chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy of the feet treated with Scrambler Therapy

identity_evidence.quote: in a patient with chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy
The patient is a woman in her 70s

attribution_limitations: The initial-visit joint rating gives pain, numbness and tingling 5/10 in the right foot and 7/10 in the left, but the numbness paragraph gives numbness at presentation as 4/10 right and 5–6/10 left. Both are the pre-treatment baseline, so the numbness values conflict; pain matches the case presentation and tingling is stated only once.

The extent of pain relief is worded differently: pain significantly decreased following 3 sessions (Results), resolved entirely after 3 sessions (Discussion), near complete resolution of neuropathic pain (Discussion, no time point) and pain lowest at the final session (Figure 1 caption). These are not literal contradictions (an entire resolution is also a significant decrease), so none is quarantined.
The abstract says improvements were sustained several weeks and months after therapy; the Results say pain relief was sustained for over a month and numbness remained low in the following weeks.

The Figure 1 caption gives eight sessions and the text says fewer than the standard 10 sessions and reports numbness by session 8; these are consistent, not a conflict, but the text never states the total number of sessions delivered.

Several sentences say neuropathy or CIPN without restating that the lower extremity neuropathy is the chemotherapy-induced neuropathy; the case text calls the bilateral lower extremity neuropathy exacerbated by prior chemotherapy.

evidence.quote: Pain score of lower extremity before and after scrambler therapy.
Placement of electrodes based on dermatome distribution.

limitations: Source conflict on the baseline numbness rating: 5/10 right and 7/10 left (initial-visit joint rating with pain and tingling) versus 4/10 right and 5–6/10 left at presentation; only the four numbness ratings are review_only.

Pain relief after 3 sessions is worded as significantly decreased (Results) and resolved entirely (Discussion), with near complete resolution and lowest pain at the final session elsewhere; recorded as an ambiguity, not a conflict.
The session count is eight per the Figure 1 caption and fewer than 10 per the text, which is consistent; the Figure 1 plotted values are pixel content and are not recorded as facts.
The 3–4/10 tolerable level, outcome expectations and travel plans are patient statements; the travel plan is not recorded as done.
No supplements are listed. Figure pixels were reviewed in the separate visual target.

claims.text: A woman in her 70s had IgG multiple myeloma that initially arose from monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance in 2000. She achieved clinical remission after bortezomib/dexamethasone and lenalidomide/dexamethasone cycles, underwent an autologous bone marrow transplant in December 2020, and remains on daratumumab maintenance after discontinuing pomalidomide because of severe CIPN. Her bilateral lower extremity neuropathy had lasted 6 years with minimal benefit from several prior therapies.
